answer:
K-means++ chooses new centers in proportion to squared distance to the nearest selected center. Lloyd iterations alternate nearest-center assignments and cluster means. Empty clusters are reseeded from high-error examples; duplicate points can still make some clusters unidentifiable. Return labels recomputed against the final centers, not labels from the previous iteration. Use a local RNG and evaluate several seeds for difficult data.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** K-means minimizes $\sum_i\|x_i-\mu_{c_i}\|^2$. Assignment minimizes this objective for fixed centers; recomputing means minimizes it for fixed assignments. This alternating descent reaches a local solution, while k-means++ improves initialization by sampling proportional to squared distance from existing centers. Standardize features when their units should not dominate distances. [3](https://www.statlearning.com/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://jakevdp.github.io/PythonDataScienceHandbook/05.11-k-means.html) and [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html).
